subject: Logging controls and header obfuscation — next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Cole <samantha@carelytics.com>, Ian Morris <ian.morris@carelytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo follow-up: logging controls & trace IDs

Hi Samantha / Ian —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps related to logging and PII controls so your security team has everything for their evaluation: 

Summary of requirements we captured on the call:
- Minimum: redact obvious PII (SSNs, full credit card numbers) in both request and response logs.
- Trace identifiers: Carelytics wants a way to avoid storing raw trace IDs in logs; acceptable solutions include deterministic hashing/pepper or removing them altogether from long-term stores.
- Retention: 30 days for raw request/response payloads, longer (12 months) for anonymized audit events.
- Residency: customer logs must remain within us-east-1 unless otherwise agreed.

What we propose (high level):
1) Default field-level redaction: apply regex and schema-based scrubbing on request and response logs with per-field rules.
2) Header obfuscation: offer a toggle that obfuscates headers containing trace identifiers and cookies before they hit S3. We can provide a HMAC-with-pepper option so debugging correlation is possible without storing clear-text IDs.
3) Retention policy: generate a configurable lifecycle policy per bucket + short-term raw buffer (default 7 days for replay, up to 30 by config).
4) Evidence: attach SOC2 summary and sample redaction rule set for review (attached).

Next steps I suggest:
- Samantha/Ian: confirm whether HMAC-with-pepper is acceptable for trace IDs or if you need no persistence at all.
- Your security contact: send any required questionnaire items we should pre-fill.
- We (Jordan + Rishi): prepare a scoped statement of work & targeted POC design (redaction rules + sample workload) for your infra team.

Attachments: redaction-requirements.xlsx (redaction rule draft), SOC2-report-2025.pdf (summary).

If you prefer, we can also draft a short technical appendix that shows how the HMAC pepper key is rotated and how we can support canary logs for debugging without storing the trace unless explicitly permitted.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.com]

From: Samantha Cole <samantha@carelytics.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Ian Morris <ian.morris@carelytics.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: logging controls & trace IDs

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side after an initial internal sync: 

1) Trace IDs: Our security team prefers we do not store any reversible identifier. HMAC-with-pepper is OK only if the pepper is customer-managed and we can rotate without Redwood retaining a copy. Otherwise the safe path is to hash with a customer-supplied salt and store only the hash.

2) Retention: 30 days for raw payloads is our requirement. We might accept 90 days for anonymized metrics, but that requires an approval.

3) Residency: Must be restricted to us-east-1 for storage and processing during the POC. Cross-region replication is a blocker unless we have a contractual exception.

4) Audits: please send the SOC2 summary (we received it) and also any sample log lines that show the obfuscation in action (redacted vs. original). A sample will make it much faster for our engineers to sign off.

We can do a quick call Thursday morning to finalize the POC scope. Ian will be the technical lead.

Best,
Samantha
Head of Security & Compliance | Carelytics

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo follow-up: logging controls & trace IDs

Rishi / Lauren —

Forwarding Carelytics' clarifications. Key asks to handle in the POC and SOW:
- Customer-supplied salt/pepper for trace ID hashing (no reversible storage by Redwood).
- Hard residency requirement: process + store only in us-east-1 for the POC.
- 30-day retention for raw payloads (configurable).
- Provide 3 sample redaction transformations (headers, JSON fields, URL query params) and example before/after log lines.

Action items:
- Rishi: can engineering support a S3 lifecycle + short-term raw buffer pattern and an option to accept customer-supplied salt? Estimate dev effort and any risk flags.
- Lauren: can you prepare a commercial note on whether the residency + customer-managed key support requires a Dedicated or Private deployment commitment (we should price both). Also, any contract redlines expected around cross-region replication.

I'll draft the POC doc and sample logs once I hear from you. Carelytics wants a Thursday sync.

Thanks,
Jordan

[Attachment: log-ingest-diagram.png — diagram of buffer -> redaction -> long-term store flow]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Cole <samantha@carelytics.com>, Ian Morris <ian.morris@carelytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Logging controls and header obfuscation — next steps

Samantha / Ian —

Per our call just now, quick notes and deliverables we agreed on: 
- Deliverables by Friday EOD: scoped POC design, three example redaction transforms, and a short technical appendix describing customer-managed salt workflows. (See attachments.)
- POC environment: us-east-1 only; 30-day raw retention; anonymized metrics retained 90 days (subject to sign-off).
- Trace IDs: implement one-way hash with customer-provided salt for the POC. We will not retain any reversible mapping.
- Evidence: we attached the SOC2 summary and a sanitized sample log file (before/after) for review.

Next meeting: Thursday 10:00 AM ET (calendar invite sent).

If anything above is misstated, flag it now and we'll correct. Looking forward to the POC.

Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachments: redaction-requirements.xlsx (rules draft), SOC2-report-2025.pdf (summary), log-ingest-diagram.png (architecture), sample-logs-sanitized.txt]
